summary_paragraph: A woman with a long history of chronic abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting was admitted after a recurrence of symptoms including chills and loose stools. She had been hospitalized the prior week at another facility where she received a blood transfusion for anemia and was found to have non-bleeding esophageal ulcers on EGD. During this admission, her pain and nausea were managed initially with IV medications, but narcotics were discontinued after discussion about the lack of long-term benefit. She tolerated advancement to an oral diet and was discharged home after stabilization. Her medications were adjusted, including continuation of Nexium for gastric ulcers and addition of Emend as a rescue anti-nausea agent. She was advised to follow up with her PCP, schedule a parotid gland biopsy to evaluate for Sjogren’s syndrome, and establish care with a chronic pain clinic and psychiatry. No acute surgical or infectious cause was identified.
